3 Oct
Gameday on Main: Arkansas vs. Texas A&M General

8:00 AM| Roy Kelly Parking Garage, 200-298 E 27th Street, Bryan, TX 77803

Texas A&M is set to host Arkansas on Saturday, Oct. 3. Headed to Kyle Field for the game? Park in Historic Downtown Bryan and take advantage of the City of Bryan’s FREE gameday shuttle!

The buses run on a continuous loop between the Roy Kelly Parking Garage and Texas A&M’s Memorial Student Center starting three hours before kickoff, throughout the game and one hour after the game.

All fans are invited to enjoy Gameday on Main for pre- and post-game celebrations, or to cheer for their team off-campus with plenty of watch options throughout downtown.

Check out our gameday website at gameday.bryantx.gov for more details.

6 Oct
National Night Out General

5:00 PM| Bryan, TX

National Night Out encourages residents to step outside to mingle with their neighbors and meet local law enforcement officers, who will visit neighborhood block parties throughout the evening.

How to set up a block party:

  • Solicit help to set up a block party from a friend or neighbor.
  • If you want to block a street off make sure to get the proper permits from the city.
  • Invite all your neighbors and solicit their help.
  • Decide what kind of food you would like. Snacks, Pot Luck, someone grilling, or catered.
  • Decide if you want music. Radio, DJ, etc. (make sure not to violate the noise ordinance)
  • If you registered your National Night Out block party online, the police department will come visit with you and bring you a goodie bag.
  • If you have questions or need help call the C.O.R.E team at 979-209-5539.

20 Oct
Senior Social: Clean Eatz Presentation Parks and Recreation

10:00 AM| Neal Recreation Center, 600 N. Randolph Avenue

Adults 55 and older are invited to a Senior Social on Tuesday, Oct. 20, from 10 - 11 a.m. at Neal Recreation Center.

Learn how Clean Eatz can support the day-to-day nutritional needs of seniors in the community. The discussion will center on practical, realistic ways to maintain balanced nutrition, including convenient meal planning options, portion-controlled Grab ‘n Go meals, and how Clean Eatz café offerings can fit into a healthy lifestyle. The goal is to provide approachable, affordable solutions that make healthy eating easier and more sustainable for seniors.

This Senior Social is free.

24 Oct
Household Hazardous Waste & Computer Collection General

7:00 AM| Texas A&M University Services Building (Old TI Road), Old Ti Rd, College Station, TX 77845

Brazos County residents are invited to participate in the Twin Oaks Landfill’s Household Hazardous Waste and Computer Collection event on Saturday, Oct. 24, from 7 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the Texas A&M University Services Building. The entrance to the facility is on Harvey Road, east of Veterans Park and Athletic Complex.

The free event offers safe disposal of a wide range of household hazardous waste and will take place rain or shine. Accepted items include aerosol cans, automobile fluids, batteries, computers, cooking oil, cleaning agents, light bulbs, oil and filters, paint, chemicals, and televisions.

For more information, visit the Twin Oaks Landfill website or call 979-764-3809.

29 Oct
Mixology Class: Halloween Edition Parks and Recreation

6:00 PM| Neal Recreational Center, 600 N Randolph Ave, Bryan, TX 77803

Ever wanted to learn how to make your favorite fall cocktails at home? Sign up for this 21+ Mixology Class to learn from the pros. We have partnered with To the Walls Bar & Event Services to bring you a “Halloween” themed night of fun and learning how to become a Mixologist. Spaces are limited. Costumes are encouraged!

Our mixology events will feature two cocktails per guest. The cocktails are not overly complicated to make, but they each have a unique element, whether that be a smoked component, muddled fruit, edible glitter and more. We also provide all participants with a recipe card, koozie & pen to take home from the event! 

The class is $50 per person. Register through Oct. 23.

Trunk or Treat So Kids Can Eat Parks and Recreation

10:00 AM| Bryan High School, 3450 Campus Dr, Bryan, TX 77802

Get ready for a spook-tacular time at the 9th Annual Trunk or Treat So Kids Can Eat, benefiting the Brazos Valley Food Bank!

Admission is five canned goods per person, and Halloween costumes are encouraged.

This event is hosted by the City of Bryan’s Parks and Recreation Department and Bryan High School.
